name: Lumateperone
summary: Lumateperone, sold under the brand name Caplyta, is an atypical antipsychotic medication of the pyridopyrroloquinoxaline and butyrophenone families. It is approved for the treatment of schizophrenia as well as bipolar depression, as either monotherapy or adjunctive therapy (with lithium or valproate), and for major depressive disorder as an adjunctive therapy only (with an oral antidepressant).

pharmacology.text: Lumateperone acts as an antagonist at 5-HT2A receptors and binds to several dopamine receptors (D1, D2, and D4) with moderate affinity. It has moderate serotonin transporter reuptake inhibition, which is partly responsible for its antidepressant effect in bipolar disorder and reduction of negative symptoms of schizophrenia. It may also inhibit dopamine transporter reuptake, but more evidence is needed to confirm this.

body.says: Multiple UGTs, CYP450s, and AKR enzymes

uses.text: Lumateperone is indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults; and depressive episodes associated with bipolar I or II disorder (bipolar depression) in adults, as monotherapy and as adjunctive therapy with lithium or valproate.

sideEffects.text: The most common adverse effects (≥5%) were somnolence and dry mouth. Lumateperone is associated with a low rate of serum aminotransferase elevations during therapy, but has not been linked to instances of clinically apparent acute liver injury.

summaryZh: 盧美哌隆（英語：Lumateperone）是一種屬於吡啶嘌呤喹唑啉與丁醯苯類的非典型抗精神病藥物。適應症包括精神分裂症與雙相情緒障礙之憂鬱發作，可作為單一療法或輔助療法（與鋰鹽或丙戊酸併用）。 此外，也可作為重度憂鬱症的輔助治療藥物（與口服抗憂鬱劑併用）。
summaryZhHans: 卢美哌隆（英语：Lumateperone）是一种属于吡啶嘌呤喹唑啉与丁酰苯类的非典型抗精神病药物。适应症包括精神分裂症与双相情绪障碍之忧郁发作，可作为单一疗法或辅助疗法（与锂盐或丙戊酸并用）。 此外，也可作为重度忧郁症的辅助治疗药物（与口服抗忧郁剂并用）。

fact.en: Sold as Caplyta, lumateperone was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration in December 2019 for schizophrenia, and its use was later extended to bipolar depression.
fact.zh: 盧美哌隆以 Caplyta 為商品名販售，2019年12月獲美國食品藥物管理局核准用於思覺失調症，之後適應症擴大到雙極性憂鬱。
fact.zhHans: 卢美哌隆以 Caplyta 为商品名贩售，2019年12月获美国食品药物管理局核准用于思觉失调症，之后适应症扩大到双极性忧郁。
